rationale: PINS ALL FOUR FIELD DECLARATION SHAPES, INCLUDING THE ONE THAT NEEDED A GRAMMAR PATCH. (1) `depth::Int = 1` under `Base.@kwdef` is a DEFAULTED field: the tree is an `assignment` whose left side is a `typed_expression`, not a bare `typed_expression`, and the first analyzer version read only the latter, publishing no `contains` edge. (2) `name::String = ""` is the second defaulted field and proves the rule is not a one-node accident. (3) `value` is a BARE field, an `identifier` directly in the struct body; the same omission class. (4) `const id::Int` is a const FIELD, Julia 1.8+ syntax with NO `=`. The vendored grammar's `const_statement` required an assignment, so this line was an ERROR node and the field was invisible — the P6 grammar patch (grammar.js, 21 files fixed and 0 broken over the whole 1,985-file corpus) makes it a `const_statement` holding a `typed_expression`. The fixture is the behavioural proof of the patch: on the old build it fails to parse cleanly and the `contains WithConst -> WithConst.id` row cannot exist. The forbid row pins that a field's TYPE is not a second field and that an inner constructor's parameter is not a field.

expectRelationships.comment: FIRE (1) — defaulted field under @kwdef; the assignment's LEFT side is the typed_expression.
FIRE (2) — a second defaulted field, so the rule is not one node's accident.
FIRE (3) — a bare field, an identifier directly in the struct body.
FIRE (4) — P6's const field. This row is impossible on the pre-patch grammar: the line is an ERROR node and `id` is not a field.
A plain annotated field, present as the control for the three shapes above.
